englishTitle: "The Dictator" Pressed a Gun to an Israeli Reporter's Groin
completenessChecks: All nine body text blocks translated in order, including the source's split of one sentence ('In return / for the grand performance') across two paragraphs, which is preserved as in the Hebrew capture.
The single interviewer prompt is bold and separate.
All three hyperlinks kept on the same words (Matt Lauer clip, student festival item, Seacrest item).
Three captions translated with credits; sidebar image linearized after the body as in the Hebrew.
voiceChecks: Bogen's news-report register is kept: wire-style lead, parenthetical '(in jest, of course)', attribution tags 'Dvir recounts in a conversation with ynet'.
Nim's quoted speech is translated as published Hebrew, including the explicit sexual joke, without sanitizing.
No Nim-style narration was introduced; the piece reads as a third-party report.
decisions: 'ירד מתחת לחגורה' rendered 'went below the belt'.
'יהודי חם' rendered 'a warm Jew' to keep the Hebrew idiom's affectionate sense.
Character and film names use the established English forms: General Aladeen, Republic of Wadiya, Larry Charles, Matt Lauer, Ryan Seacrest.
Photo credit 'mct' kept lowercase as printed.
sourceProblems: The last word of the plot summary, 'וזקן', is ambiguous without vowels ('and old' or 'and a beard'); the film's plot has Aladeen lose his beard. Translated literally as 'and old' without correction; Nim may prefer a different reading.
The source's displayed time 04:37 differs from its JSON-LD timestamp; the source record notes this. Not relevant to the translation.
Baron Cohen is spelled both בארון כהן and ברון כהן in the source captions; English uses the established 'Baron Cohen' throughout.
